title: Trace shell startup without changing your account
goal: Distinguish login, interactive non-login and noninteractive child startup using an isolated HOME.
challenge: In an isolated HOME, prove which startup marker each shell reads and record login_shell plus interactive flags. Show first-readable profile precedence; do not change real learner dotfiles.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-startup.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-startup.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here
steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace; stop on error and record its absolute path. Reopening boots the disk, not these shell variables. Never use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A new private directory; no pre-existing files are changed.

steps.command:
here && fresh .bash_profile .profile .bashrc && { printf 'echo PROFILE
' > .bash_profile; printf 'echo FALLBACK
' > .profile; printf 'echo RC
' > .bashrc; }
steps.explanation: Use harmless markers. Bash reads the first available user login profile, not every profile. This profile deliberately does not source .bashrc.
steps.expected: Three small files inside this workspace.

steps.command: here && { env -i HOME="$w" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash --login -c 'echo "HOME=$HOME flags=$-"; shopt login_shell' > login.txt; cat login.txt; }
steps.explanation: A login shell reads /etc/profile and then its first readable user profile. Verify HOME remains the isolated path; stop if the system profile changes it.
steps.expected: PROFILE, login_shell on, and no FALLBACK or RC.

steps.command: here && { env -i HOME="$w" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin TERM=linux bash --noprofile --rcfile "$w/.bashrc" -ic 'echo "HOME=$HOME flags=$-"; shopt login_shell; :' > interactive.txt; cat interactive.txt; }
steps.explanation: Explicitly use this rc file for the interactive non-login child. -i appears in shell flags; login_shell is off.

steps.command: here && { env -i HOME="$w" PATH=/usr/bin:/bin bash -c 'echo "HOME=$HOME flags=$-"; shopt login_shell; :' > child.txt; cat child.txt; }
steps.explanation: A noninteractive child does not automatically read .bashrc. BASH_ENV is intentionally absent from this clean environment.
steps.expected: No user startup marker; no interactive i flag.

hints: Compare the i flag with login_shell; they are separate.
Do not edit ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile outside the workspace.
review: I retained actual output and checked the required contents, metadata or identity, not just command success.
I can explain the stated limitations, demonstrate the incorrect case, preserve originals and clean up only my recorded workspace.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 105.1. Self-reviewed and unscored: the application does not inspect guest results. No full-objective or exam-readiness claim.
